newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank calls to boost bank security.
newsitem.headline: China central bank calls to boost bank security.

text.p: China's central bank has ordered all banks to boost security to prevent financial crimes and avoid serious losses, the Financial News said on Tuesday.

Criminal cases involving fraud, robbery and theft have occurred continuously since a $10 billion letter of credit fraud case in 1993, the newspaper quoted Yin Jieyan, vice-governor of the central bank, the People's Bank of China, as saying.
This had increased the financial risks to banks and deaths and injuries of bank staff were also rising, Yin said, without giving specific figures.

Fraud involving bank deposit certificates and money orders, robbery of bank vehicles and theft inside banks as well as bank employees colluding with outside institutions to engage in fraud were among the most worrying cases, Yin said.
A more comprehensive security system should be set up in line with expansion of bank operations, he said.
About 151,000 personnel were now employed in security for the finance sectors, Yin said.
